title: Yara and the Bakery
premise: Dominic Montrose has spent a decade keeping his head down and his heart locked, running a failing café on the edge of the orchard town of Bellhaven. When his estranged grandmother's will names him co-owner of the stubborn Wren Orchard deed alongside Yara Lindqvist, the childhood friend he abandoned after one catastrophic night, the two are forced to share land, labor, and a harvest deadline neither can meet alone. As payments, weather, and old wounds close in, Dominic must choose between selling his half and staying; Yara must decide whether forgiving him means losing herself again. They save the orchard together, confess their love at the first harvest festival, and turn the deed into a shared future rather than an inheritance of grief.
about_author: August Eriksen is the pen name of a former line cook who traded kitchen shifts for quiet mornings and slow-burn love stories. Their novels center on second chances, stubborn families, and the small towns that refuse to let anyone disappear.

chapters.title: Three Missed Payments
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A brutal morning at the café: a final notice from the bank, a burnt batch of morning buns, and a customer who mistakes him for someone with his life together. He catalogs everything he's lost and decides invisibility is a strategy, not a flaw. Emotional beat: weary denial, the calm before the legal storm.

chapters.title: The Deed That Wouldn't Die
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara, now the orchard's acting manager since Gran Wren's death, receives the probate letter naming a co-heir she hasn't seen in ten years: Dominic Montrose. She rereads Gran's cryptic note—'fix it or lose it'—and drives to the café to confront him. Emotional beat: anger sharpened by grief.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The two meet at the county records office and argue over the deed's archaic joint-tenancy clause: neither can sell without the other's consent, and the estate's debts come due at harvest. They strike a hostile bargain—one season, then split the proceeds. Emotional beat: grudging truce, sparks under the hostility.

chapters.title: Pruning Season
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic moves into the orchard cottage 'temporarily' and discovers Yara runs the place on fumes and stubbornness. His pastry skills prove unexpectedly useful at the farm stand, and a late-night pruning session cracks open the first real conversation in a decade. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness.

chapters.title: What Gran Knew
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Sorting Gran Wren's attic, Yara finds letters revealing Gran orchestrated the co-inheritance deliberately—and a photograph of the night Dominic left, which Yara never fully understood. She begins to see his departure as fear rather than betrayal. Emotional beat: grief softening into curiosity.

chapters.title: Frost Warning
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. An unseasonal frost threatens the blossoms and, with them, the entire harvest—and the debt. The town rallies for an all-night burn, and working shoulder to shoulder, Dominic and Yara nearly kiss before he pulls away, terrified of repeating the past. Emotional beat: rising intimacy, self-sabotage.

chapters.title: The Night He Left
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Flashback chapter: the truth of ten years ago—Gran caught him and Yara together, threatened to disinherit Yara if she tied herself to a Montrose, and Dominic left to protect her, telling no one why. In the present, he finally tells Yara. Emotional beat: confession, devastating relief.

chapters.title: A Buyer at the Gate
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A developer offers a fortune for the orchard—enough to erase every debt and free them both. Yara is tempted until she realizes accepting means becoming Gran's opposite: someone who sells what love built. She refuses, alone, and starts planning the harvest festival as a make-or-break gamble. Emotional beat: resolve, quiet courage.

chapters.title: First Harvest
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Festival day: storms damage half the crop overnight, the bank rep arrives mid-celebration, and Dominic publicly stakes everything—his café's last funds, his name, his heart—on the orchard and on Yara. She answers in front of the whole town. Emotional beat: climax, love chosen over safety.

chapters.title: Sweetness, Kept
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Epilogue-season chapter: the harvest numbers just clear the debt, the café reopens as the Orchard Table, and Dominic forgives the person in the mirror. On the cottage porch, they amend the deed into something Gran would have approved—a home held together, not divided. Emotional beat: earned peace, found family complete.
